main.welcomeTitle: Welcome to the Mathematical Function Analyzer!
main.welcomeDescription: This program analyzes functions of the types constant, affine, quadratic, exponential, logarithmic, sine, cosine, tangent, etc. — identifying their properties and characteristics. To get started, enter the function data when prompted.
main.documentDescription: Mathematical Function Analyzer developed in JavaScript and TypeScript.
main.noHistory: There is no history yet for changes.
main.noHistoryExp: You have written only one function so far. Use “changes” to write another function.
main.settingsNote: Note: Settings may be not saved when closing
main.allSettingsDefault: All settings are already at their default values.
main.allSettingsDefaultExp: There is no need to restore.
main.wantRestoreDefault:
Do you want to restore the default settings?
Affected settings:
main.noteRestoreDefault:
Note₁: This will affect all the settings above
Note₂: This change is permanent
main.noteUnicode:
Note₁: Unicode characters are special symbols, such as: “ℝ”, “∀”, etc. Disabling will replace them with a corresponding word, such as: “Reals”, “for all”, etc.
Note₂: Not all Unicode characters will be disabled
Note₃: This setting may change some explanations
main.noteExplanations:
Note₁: Enabling will make certain messages different and include explanations, e.g.: the Delta calculation, Δ = b² - 4 · a · c, not just the result
Note₂: Not all messages have an explained version
Note₃: Disabling Unicode will show: Delta = b^2 - 4 * a * c
main.noteAccents: Note: This setting will remove all accents from words, which may cause misinterpretation
main.noteCapitalized:
Note₁: This setting will make text “normal”, i.e., the first letter of each sentence capitalized and the rest lowercase
Note₂: This setting will disable “uppercase” and “lowercase”
main.noteUppercase:
Note₁: This setting will transform all letters to uppercase
Note₂: This setting will disable “capitalized” and “lowercase”
main.noteLowercase:
Note₁: This setting will transform all letters to lowercase
Note₂: This setting will disable “capitalized” and “uppercase”
main.noteDecimalSeparator: Note₁: This setting will transform numbers with “.” into numbers with “,”, e.g.:
main.noteDecimalSeparator2:
Note₂: This is only aesthetic and will not affect calculations
Note₃: You will also be able to type numbers with “,” instead of “.”
main.noteSimpleMulti:
Note₁: This will aesthetically change polynomial expressions from: “a · x² + b · x + c” to: “ax² + bx + c”
Note₂: Disabling Unicode will transform “·” into *
Note₃: This will not affect “×”, but Unicode will transform it into *
main.noteInputConfirm: Note: Everything typed will need to be confirmed
main.noteOutputConfirm: Note: This will show a confirmation message before exiting / closing the program
main.noteErrors: Note: Disabling may cause you not to notice errors you are making
main.noteShowFunction:
Note₁: “Show function” means the function (e.g.: ax² + bx + c) will be shown at the start of menus, before the options
Note₂: The function will still be shown when option “6” (Review / Show function) is selected
main.noteDecimalPlaces:
Note₁: Too few decimal places may cause calculation errors
Note₂: Already entered numbers will be rounded to the new number of decimal places
main.noteLogPrecision:
Note₁: This may affect very small calculations involving logarithms
Note₂: You will have to literally type “1e-12”
main.noteDivisionPrecision:
Note₁: This may affect very small calculations involving divisions
Note₂: You will have to literally type “1e-12”
main.noteInteractionLimit:
Note₁: This will affect all loops, such as logarithms, menus, etc.
Note₂: This setting is useful to avoid infinite loops in the code, in case something goes wrong
main.noteLanguage: Note: This will change the entire system language.
main.noteDegrees:
Note₁: This will affect trigonometric functions, such as sine, cosine and tangent
Note₂: Enabling this will make angles be interpreted as degrees, not π radians
main.noteSettingsExit: Note: Settings may be reset upon exit.

ui.inputConfirmNote:
Note₁: If this is a variable and what was typed is not a number, it will be transformed into the variable name, not what was typed.
Note₂: These messages can be disabled in the settings, under “Input Confirmations”.
